cars.specification_market: Original W210 E55 AMG saloon, type 210.074, selected from the factory 1997–1999 reference. The archive distinguishes August 1997 pre-production from October 1997 standard production; the year field denotes introduction, not a US model year. M113 E55/113.980, 5439 cc, 260 kW at 5500 rpm and 530 Nm at 3000 rpm. Standard five-speed torque-converter automatic, rear-wheel drive and original European tyres. No later W211 supercharged specification, US 349-hp/tyre/test data, 4MATIC, later facelift equipment or inferred production total is imported.
cars.summary: The W210 E55 AMG combined an AMG-developed V8 with uprated suspension and brakes and a heavy-duty automatic drivetrain in an everyday executive saloon. Contemporary first-hand driving evidence documents a substantial dynamic transformation beyond the ordinary E-Class. Count this W210 performance-road family once; engine choices, facelifts, estate bodies and model years do not add entries.

cars.generation: MkIII original front-drive production-road sporting hatchback family
cars.variant: RS Turbo Series 1 — 1984 introduction / original 1985 base recognition
cars.specification_market: Original MkIII / Series 1 production-road programme, introduced in 1984 according to Ford’s retrospective, with base mechanical reference from manufacturer form A-5272. Actual cover stamps June 1, 1985; portal metadata instead says June 2. Neither is a photographed chassis date. Actual 1597.2 cc is kept separate from the form’s 2236.1 cc turbo-equivalent competition capacity. Five-speed main manual column only; no additional competition gearbox, alternative final drive, minimum weight, brake option or later extension is imported. Ford retrospective supplies road output in native PS, road torque and original turbo/compression details; no bhp conversion.
cars.summary: The Series 1 Escort RS Turbo carried Ford SVE development into a front-drive performance hatchback intended as a Group A competition basis. Its intercooled turbo engine, electronic boost/ignition control and standard viscous limited-slip differential distinguish the engineering from an ordinary Escort. One MkIII sporting-road family is counted; XR3i/RS1600i badges, model years and competition preparations do not add entries.

sources.title: 50 Jahre Dampf unter der Haube — RS history, July 31, 2018
sources.notes: Actual complete Escort III RS Turbo section read, explicitly credited to Ford. Documents SVE development, Group A production-basis intent, original 132 PS, 180 Nm at 3000 rpm, 8.3:1 compression, Garrett AirResearch T3 with intercooling, Bosch KE-Jetronic and standard viscous differential lock acting on the front wheels. The planned 5000 is not treated as a final production total; no absolute first-turbo-Ford or all-white-without-exceptions claim.

facts.title: Why this car belongs
facts.explanation: The Series 1 Escort RS Turbo carried Ford SVE development into a front-drive performance hatchback intended as a Group A competition basis. Its intercooled turbo engine, electronic boost/ignition control and standard viscous limited-slip differential distinguish the engineering from an ordinary Escort. One MkIII sporting-road family is counted; XR3i/RS1600i badges, model years and competition preparations do not add entries.
